Telex types Vietnamese with plain letters: aa is â, ee ê, oo ô, aw ă, ow ơ, uw ư, dd đ, and a tone letter (s f r x j) comes right after its vowel. The workbench reads any piece you cut on vi_telex, but here the longest piece is not always the right one.
Four syllables in the middle carry no mark and no tone. Each one is a Vietnamese syllable, but together they only make sense in English.
A friend wanted an English idiom explained. The last four syllables ask what it means, and neither cos nor gif is English here.
